key_insight: Use random features only where the interface cuts the mesh, while keeping standard finite elements elsewhere, to solve elliptic interface problems efficiently on unfitted grids.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid unfitted-mesh strategy is well suited for engineering problems with sharp material jumps, complex or moving interfaces, and heterogeneous composites.
method: Apply standard Qp finite elements on all uncut background cells.
Use localized random feature representations on both sides of the interface only in the narrow cut-cell band.
Couple FEM and RFM through an artificial grid-aligned interface and enforce physical jumps via least-squares residuals with Schur reduction of interior FEM unknowns.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on 2D and 3D test cases with high coefficient contrasts, nonsmooth and multiple interfaces, irregular outer boundaries, and a thermal-homogenization application.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness depend on the cut-cell band coupling and constrained least-squares solve, which may require careful implementation for stability in highly complex geometries.
paper_title: A Localized Hybrid Finite Element--Random Feature Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Unfitted Meshes
